The right third of the frame is calm empty background. No box, no vials, no ampoules, no syringes, no bottles, no devices, no products anywhere, no captions, no text.

K3m_try1.what: the first try: both people in the frame
images: the real pen in a gloved hand
K3m_try1.prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic still, 16:9, soft natural daylight. The same bright treatment room, the same cosmetologist and the same patient as in the first reference image, a few minutes later, seen closer: a medium close-up of the two of them. Keep the arrangement of the first reference image: the patient is half-reclined on the white leather treatment couch, the back of her head resting on its headrest, her face turned up and slightly toward the cosmetologist, eyes closed, relaxed; the cosmetologist stands beside the couch at the left, leaning toward the patient's face.
The patient is the woman of the first reference image (late fifties, very short cropped platinum-blond hair under a white disposable cap, a plain white T-shirt; mature skin with fine lines, natural, not retouched, clean skin without make-up). The cosmetologist is the woman of the first reference image (about 30, long dark wavy hair, white uniform with thin pink piping, a pendant with a blue stone on a black cord, white disposable gloves on both hands); she looks down at the patient's cheek, calm and concentrated.
Composition: the two people are in the left part of the frame. The cosmetologist's face is at about 20 percent of the frame width, the patient's face at about 42 percent; the patient's head, her cap and the headrest end before 58 percent of the frame width. The right 42 percent of the frame is only calm softly blurred room - the pale wall and the white-framed window with green foliage outside, far out of focus; nothing else is there.
In her right hand, the one nearer to the camera, the cosmetologist holds the microneedling pen of the second reference image - exactly that device, as it looks in the gloved hand in the third reference image: the same champagne-gold body with its waist, the same faceted rose-gold ring, the same champagne front part between the ring and the short clear cartridge, the same small round button, indicator dot and flared end cap. The side of the pen with the lettering is turned away from the camera: no lettering and no text on the visible side. Do not change the device itself: the same proportions and thickness as in the photo, not thinner, not longer, not tapered, no cone, no nozzle, no cable, nothing added. She holds it like a thick pencil around the middle of its body, so that the whole pen is clearly seen from the clear cartridge to the flared end cap and her fingers do not hide the rose-gold ring. The clear cartridge end rests on the middle of the patient's cheek that faces the camera, halfway between the cheekbone and the jaw line. The third reference image shows only how this real pen looks when a gloved hand holds it against a cheek; take nothing else from it - the man of that image is not in this picture.
In her other hand she holds a slim transparent 1 ml syringe without any needle, filled with a perfectly clear colourless liquid like water, between her thumb and two fingers; its small plain plastic tip points down a few centimetres above the same cheek, close to the working end of the pen, and one clear drop hangs from the tip. Two or three tiny clear drops glisten on the skin of the cheek beside the pen's cartridge. The liquid is transparent: not golden, not white, not coloured.
The patient's eyes, nose and lips are not touched and not covered. One pen and one syringe only; nothing else in the hands. No table, no towel, no box, no bottle, no vial, no jar, no needle, no cotton pad, no second device, no blood, no redness of the skin. No text, no captions, no lettering anywhere.
K3m_try1.verdict: rejected by me: the pen stands at the corner of the mouth, the drop hangs over the nose, and the group reaches 79 percent of the frame width - under the page caption

K3n.what: the second try, composed closer: the patient's face in profile in the left half, only the cosmetologist's gloved hands in the frame; the pen comes from under the jaw line and stands on the cheek in front of the ear, the syringe comes from above
images: the real pen in a gloved hand
K3n.prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic close-up, 16:9, soft natural daylight. The same patient, the same cosmetologist and the same treatment room as in the first reference image, a few minutes later; the camera has come close to the patient's face. The patient is half-reclined on the white leather treatment couch with the back of her head on its headrest, as in the first reference image; her face is seen in profile, turned up toward the ceiling, eyes closed, relaxed, lips closed.
She is the woman of the first reference image: late fifties, very short cropped platinum-blond hair under a white disposable cap, a plain white T-shirt, mature skin with fine lines, natural, clean skin without make-up.
Composition: her face fills the left and the middle of the frame - the tip of her nose is at about 25 percent of the frame width, her closed eye at about 33 percent, the middle of her cheek at about 42 percent, her ear at about 54 percent; the back of her head with the cap ends before 64 percent of the frame width. The right 36 percent of the frame is only the white headrest and the softly blurred pale room with the white-framed window far out of focus: calm and empty, nothing else there.
Of the cosmetologist only her two hands in white disposable gloves, her forearms in the white uniform sleeves with thin pink piping and a lock of her long dark wavy hair at the top left edge are in the frame; her face is outside the frame.
Her right hand comes from the lower left, from under the patient's jaw line, and holds the microneedling pen of the second reference image - exactly that device, as it looks in the gloved hand in the third reference image: the same champagne-gold body with its waist, the same faceted rose-gold ring, the same champagne front part between the ring and the short clear cartridge, the same small round button, indicator dot and flared end cap. The side of the pen with the lettering is turned away from the camera: no lettering and no text on the visible side. Do not change the device itself: the same proportions and thickness as in the photo, not thinner, not longer, not tapered, no cone, no nozzle, no cable, nothing added. She holds it like a thick pencil around the middle of its body; the pen points diagonally up and to the right, and its clear cartridge end rests on the middle of the patient's cheek, below the cheekbone and in front of the ear - well away from her mouth and her nose: several centimetres of free cheek lie between the cartridge and the corner of her mouth. The whole pen is clearly seen from the clear cartridge to the flared end cap; the fingers do not hide the rose-gold ring. The pen does not cross her lips, her nose or her eye. The third reference image shows only how this real pen looks when a gloved hand holds it against a cheek; take nothing else from it - the man of that image is not in this picture.
Her left hand comes from above and holds a slim transparent 1 ml syringe without any needle, filled with a perfectly clear colourless liquid like water; its small plain plastic tip points down two or three centimetres above the same cheek, right next to the working end of the pen, and one clear drop hangs from the tip. Two or three tiny clear drops glisten on the skin of the cheek beside the cartridge. The liquid is transparent: not golden, not white, not coloured.
The patient's eye, nose and lips are not touched and not covered by anything. One pen and one syringe only. No table, no towel, no box, no bottle, no vial, no jar, no needle, no cotton pad, no second device, no blood, no redness of the skin. No text, no captions, no lettering anywhere.
K3n.verdict: the composition, the hands, the syringe and the drops are good (nose at 25 percent of the width, eye 35, cheek 45, ear 55, the cap ends at 73); two details of the pen differed from the real photo: the end cap was a wide flat disc and the champagne front part between the ring and the cartridge was missing

K3m.what: THE FRAME OF THE FILM: K3n with the two pen details corrected by one edit pass
K3m.prompt:
Keep the first image exactly as it is - the same woman, the same hands and gloves, the same skin, syringe, drops, disposable cap, couch, room, framing, light and colours; do not move or redraw anything else. Correct only two details of the microneedling pen so that it matches the real device shown in the second reference image:
1. The end cap at the lower left end of the pen. Make it the end cap of the real device: a short cone that widens from the body to a rim and then narrows to a small flat tip, with a thin groove where it meets the body. It must not be a wide flat disc.
2. The front of the pen. Between the faceted rose-gold ring and the clear cartridge there is a short champagne-gold section of the body that narrows toward the cartridge, exactly as in the second reference image; the clear cartridge is attached to this champagne section, not directly to the rose-gold ring.
The pen keeps its place, its angle, its champagne-gold colour, its small round button and indicator dot, and the hand that holds it; its clear cartridge still rests on the same spot of the cheek in front of the ear. No lettering on the pen. No text, no captions.
K3m.verdict: good: the pen checked against the real photo - end cap a short cone with a small flat tip, button and indicator dot, body, faceted rose-gold ring, champagne front part with its notch, clear cartridge with the needles; no lettering toward the camera (the small V mark near the end cap is not there); the rest of the frame did not change. The syringe is a clear graduated syringe with a plain tip, no needle; two drops on the cheek

Y1.what: the row of micro-channels: the still of the MITOPEN page, reused (free)

Y2m.what: the same channels, a clear solution goes down them (an edit of Y1; on MITOPEN the product is golden)
Y2m.prompt: The same illustration as in the first reference image - the same cut-away of the skin, the same row of seven thin vertical micro-channels, the same rounded cells and pink fibres, the same framing, light and empty softly blurred area on the right. Change only this: a perfectly clear, colourless solution, transparent like water, now lies as a thin glossy film on the skin surface above the channels and flows down inside every one of the seven channels as fine clear droplets with small bright highlights, filling them to their lower ends, where a soft pearly-white glow spreads gently into the surrounding tissue. The solution is transparent and colourless: not golden, not yellow, not milky, not blue. Everything else stays exactly as it is: the channels keep their place, number, width and depth. No needles, no instrument, no device, no text, no labels, no arrows, no numbers, no hands, no people.
Y2m.verdict: good: the same seven channels, clear droplets go down them, a soft pearly glow at their lower ends; the channels sit about 1.5 percent of the frame width to the left of Y1 - the clip BL takes it as a slight drift

W.from_to: K3m -> K3m (the drops and the pen at work; ends where it starts)
W.prompt: One continuous shot, no cuts; the camera stays in place with only a barely noticeable drift. The cosmetologist works with the microneedling pen on the patient's cheek: the clear drop falls from the tip of the small syringe onto the skin, and with short gentle stamping touches she moves the pen step by step along the cheek, then a few steps across it, crisscross; another clear drop falls beside the pen. The pen itself does not change its shape, colour or size; the syringe stays a slim clear syringe without a needle. The patient lies calm with her eyes closed and breathes quietly. Natural small movements, soft daylight. The shot ends in the same position as it begins. No text, no captions.

BL.from_to: Y1 -> Y2m (the clear solution goes down the micro-channels)
BL.prompt: One continuous shot, no cuts; the camera stays almost still with a barely noticeable slow drift. The scientific illustration of the skin cut-away with the row of thin vertical micro-channels stays as it is. A clear colourless solution, transparent like water, spreads as a thin glossy film over the skin surface above the channels and then flows slowly down inside each channel as fine clear droplets with small bright highlights, one channel after another, until all the channels are filled to their lower ends and a soft pearly-white glow spreads gently into the tissue around them. The channels keep their place, number and depth. No needles, no instruments, no text, no labels, no arrows.
